title: DomainConfig
description: Full configuration for one domain. One JSON file = one domain. Wire it in app/domains/index.ts — no other files need changing.

$schema.description: Points to this schema file for editor validation. Set to './schema.json'.

entityTypes.description: All entity type IDs in this domain. Used as the canonical list throughout the engine. Order does not matter here — use fillOrder and selectionOrder for ordering.

entityTypeLabels.description: Display names for each entity type. Keys must match entityTypes.

fillOrder.description: Order entity slots appear in the BOM output. Also the fallback iteration order for the engine if selectionOrder is omitted.

selectionOrder.description: Order the backtrack fill selects core entities (not including anchorType or capacityType). These are filled share-by-share. Omit to use fillOrder.

maxPerType.description: Hard cap on quantity per entity type. Types not listed here default to 1 (or use dynamicMaxPerType). Use for types that are always a single unit.

dynamicMaxPerType.description: For entity types whose slot count depends on another entity's attribute (e.g., RAM slots from motherboard). Key = the entity type whose count is dynamic.

requiredTypes.description: Entity types that must be present for a build to be valid. Missing types produce an error validation issue.

anchorType.description: The 'hero' entity that defines the tier of the whole build. The engine tries every anchor candidate and picks the best-fitting combination. Gets the largest share of the budget. If omitted, defaults to fillOrder[0].

capacityType.description: Entity type that acts as a capacity constraint (e.g., PSU for power). The engine selects the cheapest item whose capacityAttribute >= totalLoad / capacityFactor. If omitted, no capacity constraint is applied.

capacityAttribute.description: Attribute on the capacityType entity that holds its rated capacity (e.g., watt_output for PSU). Required when capacityType is set.

loadAttributes.description: Attribute names that represent load/consumption on non-capacity entities. The engine reads the first non-null attribute from this list per entity. Required when capacityType is set.

capacityFactor.description: Safety multiplier for capacity selection. minCapacity = totalLoad / capacityFactor. 0.8 means the chosen PSU can handle 125% of actual draw (80% rule).

aggregateGuardTypes.description: Entity types that participate in aggregate constraint checking during backtrack fill. The engine re-checks aggregate rules whenever one of these types changes.

primary.description: Rule code to show as the main aggregate meter in the UI (e.g., power capacity bar).

safety.description: Rule code for the secondary safety meter (e.g., 80% power rule). Null to hide.

aggregateDisplay.description: Which aggregate rules to display as meters in the simulation UI.

costAttribute.description: Key in entity.attributes that holds the unit cost. The engine reads this for all budget calculations.

costColumn.description: Database column name for unit cost. Used in SQL queries (SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY). Must match the actual DB schema column. Defaults to 'unit_cost'.

costPrecision.description: Decimal places for cost display and rounding. 0 = whole numbers (THB), 2 = cents.

publishedStatus.description: The entity status value that means 'available for suggestion'. Only entities with this status are included in the pool. Defaults to 'published'.

fillStrategy.description: Name of the fill algorithm to use. Must match a registered strategy in app/engine/strategies/index.ts. Currently only 'backtrack' is available.

fetchLimits.description: How many DB rows to fetch per category. Higher values improve suggestion quality at the cost of more D1 row reads.

budgetPlan.description: RuleFlow2 module that calculates anchorTarget from effectiveBudget and entityCount. If omitted, uses the default formula: round(effectiveBudget * ceil(entityCount/2) / entityCount).

postFillTypes.description: Extra fill phases that run after backtrack fill completes. Use for entities that are selected in tiers (e.g., SSD: cheap first, upgrade later if budget allows).

tierRules.description: Cross-entity tier constraints. If a provider entity (e.g., high-end GPU) is selected, it requires a matching tier on another entity type (e.g., high-cache CPU). Evaluated during fill.

rules.description: All compatibility rules for this domain. Supports two check types: pairwise (entity vs entity) and aggregate (sum/count across types vs a capacity).

source_type.description: Entity type that owns the slot count attribute (e.g., 'motherboard').

source_attribute.description: Attribute on source_type that holds the slot count (e.g., 'ram_slots').

capacity_attribute.description: Attribute on the dynamic entity that counts how many slots one unit consumes (e.g., 'modules' for a dual-channel RAM kit).

sort_attribute.description: Attribute used to sort candidates of this type during selection (e.g., 'capacity_gb'). Highest value preferred.

fallback.description: Max quantity to use when source_type has no item selected yet.

type.description: Entity type this phase applies to.

preferAttribute.description: Attribute to optimise for (highest value wins within budget).

maxAttrValue.description: Upper bound filter on preferAttribute. Selects the best item at or below this value (e.g., SSD ≤512 GB).

minAttrValue.description: Lower bound filter on preferAttribute. Selects the best item at or above this value (e.g., SSD ≥1000 GB).

upgradeExisting.description: false = initial fill of empty slot. true = upgrade an already-filled slot if budget remains.

anchor.description: Max rows fetched for anchorType (top-N by cost descending). Higher = wider anchor selection.

anchorNear.description: Extra rows for anchor fetched near the calculated anchorTarget price point.

core.description: Max rows per core entity type (top-N by cost descending).

coreCheap.description: Extra cheap rows per core entity type (top-N by cost ascending).

name.description: Unique identifier for this tier rule.

entity_type.description: Entity type that triggers this rule when its condition matches.

condition.description: JSON Logic condition evaluated on the provider entity. Use { 'var': 'attributes.X' } to access attributes.

entity_type.description: Entity type that must satisfy this condition when provider matches.

condition.description: JSON Logic condition evaluated on each candidate of this type. Candidates failing this condition are excluded from selection.

id.description: Unique integer ID within this domain. Used as cache key.

code.description: Unique string code (SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE). Matches aggregateDisplay keys.

name.description: Human-readable rule name shown in error detail.

check_type.description: pairwise = evaluate one entity pair at a time. aggregate = sum/count across multiple entities and compare to a capacity.

severity.description: error = blocks valid build. warning = shown but build is still valid. info = informational only.

priority.description: Evaluation order — higher number runs first.

is_active.description: Set false to disable a rule without removing it.

message.description: Displayed message when rule fails. Use :source.attributes.X, :target.attributes.X, :aggregate_value, :capacity_value, :utilization_pct as interpolation tokens.

resolution.description: Suggested fix shown to the user.

scope.description: Required for check_type=pairwise. Defines which entity pairs to evaluate.

condition.description: Pairwise rules: JSON Logic object ({ '==': [...] }). Aggregate rules: object with top-level 'aggregate' key.

match_by.description: shared_attribute: both entities share the same attribute key and it must match. attribute_pair: source and target have different attribute keys that must match. attribute_range: source attribute must fall within target attribute range.

attribute_key.description: Used with shared_attribute: the attribute key checked on both entities.

source_attribute.description: Used with attribute_pair/range: attribute on the source entity.

target_attribute.description: Used with attribute_pair/range: attribute on the target entity.

source_types.description: Filter: only evaluate entities of these types as source. Empty = all types.

target_types.description: Filter: only evaluate entities of these types as target.

JsonLogicCondition.description: JSON Logic expression. Evaluates to true/false. Available operators: ==, !=, >, >=, <, <=, and, or, not, in, var. Access entity attributes with { 'var': 'source.attributes.X' } or { 'var': 'target.attributes.X' }.

AggregateCondition.description: For aggregate rules. Computes a value across multiple entities and compares it to a capacity.

fallback_attributes.description: Try these attributes if primary is null (e.g., ['tdp_w']).

from_types.description: Entity types to include. Use ['*'] for all types.

exclude_types.description: Entity types to exclude even if matched by from_types.

multiply_by_quantity.description: true = multiply attribute value by slot quantity (e.g., 2× RAM kits).

entity_type.description: entity_attribute mode: which entity type holds the capacity.

attribute.description: entity_attribute mode: which attribute holds the capacity value.

safety_factor.description: Multiply capacity by this factor before comparing (e.g., 0.8 for 80% rule).

constraint_key.description: simulation_constraint mode: key from the constraints map passed to validateItems.

value.description: fixed_value mode: compare against this literal value.

Module.description: RuleFlow2 module for declarative formula evaluation. Used in budgetPlan to express the anchor target calculation without hardcoded TypeScript.

inputs.description: Input variable declarations. All must be provided at runtime.

outputs.description: Output variable names. Must match the 'out' fields of blocks.

blocks.description: Computation steps. Currently only formula blocks are supported.

FormulaBlock.description: A single formula computation. Use $varName to reference inputs or prior block outputs.

expr.description: Expression string. Reference variables with $name. Functions: round(), ceil(), floor(), min(), max(), abs().
